title: Display your first message with Python
description: Use the print() command to show a message on the screen. For example, you can write print("Hello, World!") or print("My name is Ayaan"). You may choose your own words.
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Use print(...) with any text or value. The exact words do not matter.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: This task gives you practice with your first python program. The reference solution is only one example; other working approaches are accepted when they use the required Python feature.
commonMistakes: Check brackets and quotes, use the correct indentation, and make sure you actually use the Python feature asked for in the task.

validation.feedback: Use print(...) with any text or value. The exact words do not matter.

title: Write a comment, then display a message
description: A comment is a note for people reading your code. Start a line with # to write a comment, then use print() on another line to show any message you like.

title: Display two messages on separate lines
description: Use print() two times to show two messages. Put one print() statement on each line. You can choose both messages, such as "Hello" and "Welcome".
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Your program should display at least two non-empty lines.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: This task gives you practice with print two lines. The reference solution is only one example; other working approaches are accepted when they use the required Python feature.
commonMistakes: Check brackets and quotes, use the correct indentation, and make sure you actually use the Python feature asked for in the task.

validation.feedback: Your program should display at least two non-empty lines.
